lesson.title: The Balance of Power
lesson.summary: How countries prevent a single nation from dominating the international system.

blocks.text: What is the balance of power?
The balance of power is a principle of international politics stating that no nation should become powerful enough to dominate all others.
When a country grows rapidly, others tend to react by forming alliances, increasing military spending, or creating containment mechanisms.
Power is not something one possesses in isolation, but something that exists in relation to others.
This mechanism helps explain why major wars often arise when the balance is broken — and why international alliances are so common.

items: Reduces the risk of total domination

cards.front: What is the balance of power?
cards.back: The idea that no nation should concentrate enough power to dominate all others.

cards.front: How do countries react to a rising rival?
cards.back: By forming alliances, strengthening military capabilities, or adopting containment policies.

cards.front: What is the main goal of the balance of power?
cards.back: To maintain stability and prevent hegemonies in the international system.

quiz.question: What is the main purpose of the balance of power?
options: Prevent a single country from dominating others
quiz.explanation: The balance of power seeks to prevent hegemonies, not eliminate conflicts or create global governments.

quiz.question: Which of these actions is NOT typical of a balance of power policy?
quiz.explanation: Permanent neutrality is not an active response to a power imbalance.
